positions.name: Micron Technology, Inc.
positions.catalyst: Overnight WSJ report that the U.S. government has formally WARNED Apple not to source memory chips from Chinese suppliers (CXMT/YMTC) — a direct reversal of the weekend report that Washington might ALLOW it, which is what crushed the memory complex on Monday (SNDK -9%, MU -5.8% to -7%, WDC -7%). The bear headline that caused the drawdown has been invalidated inside 24 hours, and the tape is confirming: MU +2.5% premarket to $933.10 (prev close $910.43), SNDK +3.7%, STX +3.3%, WDC +2.7%, QQQ +0.93% vs SPY +0.45% — a clean memory-led risk-on rotation, not a broad beta bounce.
positions.driver: Three stacked drivers into a ~24h hold. (1) Headline reversal: Monday's selloff was a policy scare, now reversed by the White House pushing Apple AWAY from Chinese memory — structurally bullish for MU, an incumbent Apple DRAM/NAND supplier, and sell-side (Lynx) already called Monday's move an overreaction on the grounds that CXMT cannot qualify for iPhone and YMTC has committed its newest NAND domestically. (2) Pricing upcycle intact: TrendForce sees Q3-26 conventional DRAM contract prices +13-18% q/q and NAND +10-15%; Samsung is pushing ~20% q/q DRAM ASP hikes and SK hynix has scrapped price ceilings on long-term supply agreements. (3) Positioning: NVDA reports FQ2 Wednesday Aug 26 AFTER the close — memory names typically get bid into that print, and this book rotates out Wednesday MORNING, capturing the anticipation drift while exiting BEFORE the binary event. Chose MU over SNDK deliberately: SNDK offers more raw upside but MU is the mega-cap, most-liquid expression, is the least premarket-extended of the group (+2.5% vs SNDK +3.7%, nowhere near the 8-10% chase threshold), and still trades well below Friday's level, leaving gap-fill room. Given the book is -22.8% from inception, downside protection is weighted over raw beta.
positions.risks: MU-specific Netlist patent litigation is a live, unresolved overhang that resurfaced in Monday's coverage. MU is a high-volatility name: Monday's intraday range alone was $887.61-$942.52 (~6%), so the 6% stop at $877.11 sits only ~1.2% below Monday's low and can be taken out on noise rather than thesis failure. The Apple/China policy story is headline-driven and could flip a third time ahead of Xi's U.S. visit. Broader risk: pre-NVDA de-risking can resume at any point this week, and Jackson Hole runs Aug 27-29 — a hawkish drift in rates has already hit memory once this month (Aug 18). Samsung's disappointing shareholder-return plan (-9% Monday) shows the memory trade is crowded and reacts violently to non-fundamental news. Dick's Sporting Goods (DKS) reports at 7:00am ET, after this run — deliberately not traded, unknowable at run time.
